findings.reason: declaring s44 and s45 as depending on s43 changes dispatch order and stops a worker building §44's single-call refactor against code §43 is about to change.
findings.text: §43, §44 and §45 are all `implementable` and all declare `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` in their write paths, but `plan-section-depends-on` lists only s37->s36, s39->s37 and s42->s41, so the queue cannot hold either of the later two behind §43; §43 rewrites the tie-break inside `review_coverage` (plan_review.py near lines 1024-1039) and §44 requires the write response and admission to compute coverage "through one call with the same inputs", which is the same function and the same `changes` mapping §43's third case reads — a worker dispatched to §44 before §43 lands builds against a `review_coverage` about to be rewritten, and §43's own line anchors move under it

findings.reason: naming the snapshot as the reader the stop hook uses is what tells the worker there are two producers to change rather than one.
findings.text: §46 names `obligations.py` (near line 2588) as the reading that "still listed the request as queued-awaiting-session", but its Why says what actually blocked the turn was "the stop hook", and that hook reaches `reckon.crew.obligation_snapshot` (`reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:123`), whose own `if row.get("session_refusal")` branch at `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:1460` rebuilds `QUEUED_AWAITING_SESSION_DUTY_KIND` independently of the obligations derivation — the caller the fix must reach is named nowhere in the section

findings.reason: without a case that reads the published snapshot, the node can pass its own gate and leave the reported defect in place.
findings.text: §46's done-when asserts only that "the request is listed among the waits" on the obligations reading, so a worker who changes `reckon/crew/obligations.py` alone satisfies all three of its stated checks while `obligation_snapshot.py:1460` — the branch the stop hook reads — still emits the `queued-awaiting-session` duty, which is exactly the symptom the section was written for

findings.reason: adding a control that holds on a differently-derived unit set is what makes the second case able to fail.
findings.text: §44's second case requires the held request to name "the same units" as the write response, but neither stated control falsifies that assertion: "giving admission its own coverage call" makes the first case hold (so the second still passes) and "treating an unmeasured change as covered in one reader alone" only reaches the third, so an implementation that holds with a wrong or empty unit set passes the whole done-when

findings.reason: both symbols are named in the section, so a worker resolves them by search and its path is unchanged; refreshing the numbers is cheap but alters no mechanism.
findings.text: §45 cites `_WRITE_PATHS_SENTENCE` at "near line 4712" and its section reader at "near line 4741", but at the base revision they are at `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:4908` and `:4937`; §44 likewise cites the routing refusal at "near line 2744" while the `uncovered units` message it quotes is at `reckon/crew/routing.py:2795` (the `review_coverage` call at `:2768`), and line 2744 sits beside a different refusal

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §45's two line citations are ~196 lines stale and §44 cites the routing refusal 50 lines above where it is raised, though every cited symbol resolves by name.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §46's done-when measures only the obligations derivation while the reported symptom is the stop hook, which reads `reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py`; §44's second case carries no negative control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §44 sends its reproduction inputs to the run directory, which is the durable crew run path this plan's other sections use; §45 and §46 leave their gate logs to the same run-directory convention the armed suite already writes.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach the proposed test filenames or symbols, and no comment restates a tracker entry.
